title: AI-generated content is weakening default trust in influencers and brands while increasing demand for human credibility and demonstrated expertise
source_unit: Gartner Marketing survey and September 2026 public Q&A on AI-generated marketing content

observations.period: May-June 2026 survey; AI and influencer reliance

influencer_reliance_decline.unit: percent saying they rely less on influencers for shopping information and recommendations because of AI-generated content

real_people_reliance_increase.unit: percent saying they rely more on real people for shopping information and recommendations because of AI-generated content

trust_reassessment.value: consumers are becoming more selective about which sources and content they trust as AI-generated material becomes more prevalent

observations.method: Gartner survey of 1,006 U.S. consumers conducted May-June 2026; findings are reported in a Gartner newsroom Q&A, with no public questionnaire or weighting details beyond the published sample.
observations.uncertainty: This is a U.S. consumer survey and cannot establish global behavior, causal effects of AI exposure, or whether stated reliance changes lead to actual purchases or source switching.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers using influencers, real people, brands, social platforms, and AI-mediated content for product discovery and recommendations.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reduced influencer reliance may reflect a shift toward more trustworthy sources, but it may also increase dependence on opaque recommendation systems, private communities, or established brands.

observations.period: May-June 2026 survey; perceived brand AI saturation

too_much_ai_marketing.unit: percent believing brands are producing too much AI-generated content in marketing materials

brand_message_trust_loss.unit: percent saying AI-generated content has made them less trusting of brand messaging overall

ai_skepticism.value: consumers are not rejecting AI outright but are becoming more selective about content quality, usefulness, and source credibility

observations.method: Gartner survey evidence summarized in the public release; perceived content saturation and trust are self-reported attitudes.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not distinguish all forms of AI-generated content, measure exposure frequency, or show whether skepticism improves discernment or simply lowers trust across the information environment.
observations.subgroup: Consumers exposed to brand, creator-led, and social-media marketing content in AI-saturated channels.
observations.counterinterpretation: Content volume may matter less than disclosure, quality, relevance, and accountability; thoughtful AI use could improve consumer experience without producing the same distrust as low-effort output.

observations.period: 2026; authenticity and expertise as marketing response

denominator.unit: Gartner analyst interpretation of the published survey

credibility_priorities.value: credibility, transparency, demonstrated expertise, useful content, and distinctive human perspectives

quality_over_quantity.value: consumers signal that quality matters more than simply increasing content output

human_perspective.value: human expertise and authentic perspectives remain important for building trust

observations.method: Analyst interpretation and marketing guidance accompanying the Gartner survey; this is not a separate experimental test of the recommended practices.
observations.uncertainty: Recommendations describe plausible trust-building mechanisms but do not demonstrate that any specific transparency or expertise intervention causes higher trust or conversion.
observations.subgroup: Brand marketers, influencers, creators, consumers, platforms, and audiences evaluating provenance and expertise.
observations.counterinterpretation: Human presentation can also be staged, sponsored, or misleading; authenticity signals require accountability and evidence rather than merely a human face.

denominator.unit: Gartner public analysis of AI-generated content across brand, creator, and social channels

content_saturation.value: AI-generated content is described as increasing across brand, creator-led, and social-media channels

decision_signal.value: consumers are reassessing who and what they trust rather than rejecting AI categorically

platform_consequence.value: provenance, disclosure, relevance, and demonstrated expertise become more important as content volume grows

observations.method: Public Gartner analyst discussion based on the survey and marketing-channel analysis; no platform-level exposure or engagement logs are reported.
observations.uncertainty: The release cannot identify how algorithmic ranking, socioeconomic position, age, or media literacy mediate the observed trust response.
observations.subgroup: Consumers with different levels of digital literacy, platform dependence, purchasing power, and access to trusted human expertise.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI saturation may eventually produce better provenance standards and more deliberate source evaluation, but it may also deepen unequal information burdens for people with less time or capacity to verify claims.

related_sources.claim: Kearney Future Consumer study provides complementary evidence on trust, verification workload, AI-mediated time, and synthetic social connection.
Edelman Trust Barometer provides complementary institutional and intergroup trust context.
WEF emerging-technology foresight provides complementary governance and trust/access context for AI systems.

boundary: This record adds a platform-and-marketing trust route linking AI-generated content, influencer reliance, brand credibility, human expertise, provenance, and information burden. It uses a Gartner U.S. consumer survey and analyst interpretation, not platform telemetry, a representative global sample, a causal experiment, or proof that skepticism leads to better decisions.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Gartner newsroom page was reviewed for survey timing, sample size, reported percentages, analyst interpretation, and boundaries around AI-generated brand, influencer, and social-media content.
